151	the Z-Wave JS *device* diagnostics (`userIdStatus[5]`), which the reporter was
152	told to skip. Do not re-assert the mechanism without that.

155	three paths answer "is this slot occupied?" and the cached one differs.
156	`getCredential` (fresh, `AccessControl.ts:960`) and the bulk branch of
157	`#getAllCredentials_UC` (`:1884`) reject only Available/StatusNotAvailable and
158	return `data: userCode` even when it is `""`. `#getCredentialCached_UC`

160	and "occupied, value unknown" into one return value.

163	has no such state. `UserCodeCCReport.from` requires payload >= 6 bytes (>= 4
164	code bytes) whenever status is occupied; a 2-byte report is legal only for
165	Available/StatusNotAvailable. Locks that withhold send filler (zeros ->
166	parsed to `""` after trailing-zero stripping, or asterisks), and LCM's

168	the unified `CredentialData`, not a protocol gap.

170	**Root cause (candidate 2, the gap PR #1408 closes):** when the device reports
171	`userIdStatus[slot]` occupied but withholds/masks the code value,
172	node-zwave-js's `#getCredentialCached_UC` omits the credential entirely.

174	`SlotCredential.empty()` and only overlays *credentials*, so "user exists,
175	value unknown" collapses to `empty()`. `_pin_state` already maps a withheld
176	value to `unreadable()` — the credential just never reaches it.
177	
178	**Fix shape:** provider-side in `zwave_js.async_get_users` — for User Code CC
179	nodes, synthesize an `unreadable()` PIN credential for any slot whose
180	`userIdStatus` is in-use but that produced no credential. `_uc_slot_in_use()`
181	already reads exactly that value, and `get_usercode`/`ATTR_IN_USE`/
182	`NotFoundError` are already imported.
183	
184	**Do NOT fix this in `_project_users_to_slots`:** "tagged user exists with no
185	PIN credential" is a *legitimate* state under the persistent-user-anchor
186	lifecycle (see `_base.py:1232`) meaning the slot is genuinely cleared. Mapping
187	it to `unreadable()` in the base would make a cleared slot never confirm.
188	
189	**Fixed in PR #1408** (branch `fix/1397-uc-occupied-slot-unreadable`):
190	`ZWaveJSLock.async_get_usercodes` overrides the projection and calls
191	`_overlay_uc_occupancy`, upgrading `empty` -> `unreadable` for any slot whose
192	User Code CC `in_use` is `True`. Landed with 4 new tests; repo still at 100%.
193	
194	**Design trap hit on the way — see
195	[[feedback-read-repair-not-in-shared-read]].** The first attempt put the
196	fallback in `async_get_users` and synthesized an owning `User`. That broke 3
197	unrelated tests: `async_set_user`'s legacy-adoption scan (untagged user at
198	`user_id == slot`) adopted the synthesized user and turned a user CREATE into
199	an UPDATE. `async_get_users` feeds the *write* paths too; the projection is the
200	only read-only seam.
201	
202	**Still open (low priority, no longer blocking):** why slots 1-4 read back in
203	cleartext if this lock withholds values — possibly stale value-DB entries from
204	the legacy property path, cf. [[project-hard-refresh-scrubs-stale-usercode]].
205	See [[project-uc-report-shim]] for the surrounding UC bridge.

  (`zwave_js.py:366`) needs `in_use is True`, and the stale value DB says
  Available. Matches "I still see the same error."
- **Driver upgrade will not fix it** — see the version analysis below; none
  of #8884/#8927/#8879/#8866 touch a timed-out verification GET.

**PR #1410** (branch `fix/1397-surface-link-health`) makes the next report of
this shape self-diagnosing: optional `BaseLock.describe_link_health()` (default
None) whose sentence is appended to the suspension repair; zwave_js quotes
`node.statistics` counters. Purely descriptive — no thresholds (a FLiRS lock's
~1s rtt is normal beam latency, so any cutoff would misfire across device
classes), no new state, no control-flow change. Does NOT close #1397.

Reporter's remedy: **fix the mesh** (rtt >1s, repeaterRSSI -88, 49% timeouts
is a marginal link). LCM's own gap: `coordinator.unreachable` is binary and
the node is `Alive`, so the degraded-lock path (`_base.py:542`) never
engages for a node that is reachable but drops half its responses. Suspending
a slot for that is the wrong outcome — cf. [[project-degraded-lock-followups]]
and [[feedback-retry-recovery-signal-must-match-failure]].

**Superseded 2026-08-13 reading (kept for the reasoning trail):** Front Door Lock (Kwikset **HC620**, fw 7.21.0,
node 2, User Code CC **v2**, no User Credential CC; driver **15.24.2**,
server 3.9.0):

```
slot 1-4 : userIdStatus=1 Enabled   userCode=<redacted>   <- LCM reads these fine
slot 5   : userIdStatus=0 Available userCode=''           <- the reported slot
slot 7   : userIdStatus=0 Available userCode=<redacted>   <- phantom, cf #1307
slot 6,8,9,10,44-46,51-53,170-172 : Available, ''
```

So **`userIdStatus[5]` is `Available`**: the lock itself reports slot 5 empty.
`#getAllCredentials_UC` (`AccessControl.ts:1858`) is a real device read
(`api.get(userId, true)`), so the value DB reflects what the lock answered —
this is not driver-cache staleness. Consequences:

- **PR #1408 / 4.4.2 provably cannot help this reporter.**
  `_overlay_uc_occupancy` (`zwave_js.py:366`) does
  `if code_slot.get(ATTR_IN_USE) is not True: continue`, and `in_use` is
  False here. Matches their "I still see the same error" after updating.
- **The docstring assumption at `zwave_js.py:625-635` is falsified in the
  field.** It justifies mapping `credential_rejected_unknown` -> OPTIMISTIC
  with "there the write actually succeeded (`userIdStatus` -> Enabled)".
  This lock returns ERROR_UNKNOWN *and* leaves `userIdStatus` Available.
  So OPTIMISTIC is being granted to a write that genuinely did not land.
- Fix shape is the one the maintainer predicted for this branch: **stop
  letting a slot that can never be confirmed run all the way to
  suspension** — not a read-projection change. Suspension logic lives in
  `domain/sync.py:505 _suspend_slot` / `_code_suspend_target`.
- Reporter's driver **15.24.2 is below both documented thresholds** —
  15.24.3 (UC dispatch #8879, delete cache-clear #8866, capability
  interview) and 15.25.2 (supervised UC writes persist, #8927). Worth
  having them update before anything else; `zwave_js.py:427` already
  tells users to, but only when `num_slots == 0`.
- Still unexplained (needs their debug logs): why the write does not land
  while the PIN reportedly works on the keypad. Confirm with the reporter
  that they actually tested slot 5's PIN on the keypad — the phrase "it
  does work" in the report is ambiguous.

**CAUTION — the mechanism below was the competing hypothesis and is NOT
#1397's cause (kept for the #1408 rationale, which stands on its own).** A later
trace through node-zwave-js `upstream/master` found no normal path that
produces "userIdStatus occupied + userCode undefined": `persistUserCode`
writes status and code together or removes both; `#persistCachedUserCode`
writes both; `setUser` on a UC lock *throws* rather than create a codeless
user; and `secret: true` on `userCode` only means "omit from value logs"
(`core/src/values/Metadata.ts:74`) — it does NOT exclude the value from the
disk cache, so it survives restarts. If that state is unreachable, slot 5's
cached lookup returned undefined because **status is `Available`**, in which
case `_uc_slot_in_use` is False and PR #1408 does not fire. Settling it needs
the Z-Wave JS *device* diagnostics (`userIdStatus[5]`), which the reporter was
told to skip. Do not re-assert the mechanism without that.

**The real, verified upstream inconsistency (worth an issue regardless):**
three paths answer "is this slot occupied?" and the cached one differs.
`getCredential` (fresh, `AccessControl.ts:960`) and the bulk branch of
`#getAllCredentials_UC` (`:1884`) reject only Available/StatusNotAvailable and
return `data: userCode` even when it is `""`. `#getCredentialCached_UC`
(`:2081`) adds `if (data == undefined) return undefined`, collapsing "empty"
and "occupied, value unknown" into one return value.

**Wire-level answer to "what should the CC return":** nothing — the encoding
has no such state. `UserCodeCCReport.from` requires payload >= 6 bytes (>= 4
code bytes) whenever status is occupied; a 2-byte report is legal only for
Available/StatusNotAvailable. Locks that withhold send filler (zeros ->
parsed to `""` after trailing-zero stripping, or asterisks), and LCM's
`_pin_state` already maps both to `unreadable`. So it is a model-level gap in
the unified `CredentialData`, not a protocol gap.

**Root cause (candidate 2, the gap PR #1408 closes):** when the device reports
`userIdStatus[slot]` occupied but withholds/masks the code value,
node-zwave-js's `#getCredentialCached_UC` omits the credential entirely.
`_project_users_to_slots` (`_base.py:1321`) starts every managed slot at
`SlotCredential.empty()` and only overlays *credentials*, so "user exists,
value unknown" collapses to `empty()`. `_pin_state` already maps a withheld
value to `unreadable()` — the credential just never reaches it.

**Fix shape:** provider-side in `zwave_js.async_get_users` — for User Code CC
nodes, synthesize an `unreadable()` PIN credential for any slot whose
`userIdStatus` is in-use but that produced no credential. `_uc_slot_in_use()`
already reads exactly that value, and `get_usercode`/`ATTR_IN_USE`/
`NotFoundError` are already imported.

**Do NOT fix this in `_project_users_to_slots`:** "tagged user exists with no
PIN credential" is a *legitimate* state under the persistent-user-anchor
lifecycle (see `_base.py:1232`) meaning the slot is genuinely cleared. Mapping
it to `unreadable()` in the base would make a cleared slot never confirm.

**Fixed in PR #1408** (branch `fix/1397-uc-occupied-slot-unreadable`):
`ZWaveJSLock.async_get_usercodes` overrides the projection and calls
`_overlay_uc_occupancy`, upgrading `empty` -> `unreadable` for any slot whose
User Code CC `in_use` is `True`. Landed with 4 new tests; repo still at 100%.

**Design trap hit on the way — see
[[feedback-read-repair-not-in-shared-read]].** The first attempt put the
fallback in `async_get_users` and synthesized an owning `User`. That broke 3
unrelated tests: `async_set_user`'s legacy-adoption scan (untagged user at
`user_id == slot`) adopted the synthesized user and turned a user CREATE into
an UPDATE. `async_get_users` feeds the *write* paths too; the projection is the
only read-only seam.

**Still open (low priority, no longer blocking):** why slots 1-4 read back in
cleartext if this lock withholds values — possibly stale value-DB entries from
the legacy property path, cf. [[project-hard-refresh-scrubs-stale-usercode]].
See [[project-uc-report-shim]] for the surrounding UC bridge.

        Read one slot back from the device so the driver's cache converges.

        Pre-15.25.2 drivers never persist a supervised User Code CC write
        to the value database (success) and never re-read the slot after a
        failure, so every later cached read -- including LCM's own initial
        load after a restart -- serves the pre-write state. This fresh
        single-slot read through the unified API forces the driver to

        report repairs the value database and doubles as a push through
        the report shim above; on a User Credential CC lock the driver
        dispatches natively and the read is merely redundant.

        returns or raises on its own evidence), so a failed read must not
        change the outcome -- the next hard refresh or sync tick reconciles
        instead.

I have the full picture now. Here's my read on where #1307 stands.

## TL;DR

There's no LCM bug in the new report. flyize's failed clear is the **same root cause as #1397: their Z-Wave mesh drops ~half of all read responses to these locks**, and every path that could resolve the slot-10 phantom depends on a read succeeding. LCM behaved exactly as designed — it attempted the delete, the driver couldn't verify it, and the repair honestly stayed open.

## The trace

The screenshot error is `unmanaged_code_clear_failed` with the error text filled in from HA core's `credential_rejected_unknown` exception ("The device rejected the credential without giving a reason") — that's the driver returning `ERROR_UNKNOWN`. The chain:

1. The repair's "clear" step (`repairs.py:62`) → `async_internal_clear_usercode` → provider `async_delete_credential` (`providers/zwave_js.py:698`) → HA's `lock_helpers.async_delete_credential`.
2. The Kwikset 620 advertises **no Supervision CC**, so the driver sends the clear and then must verify by reading the slot back. On this mesh the verification GET times out roughly half the time → driver returns `ERROR_UNKNOWN` → HA raises `credential_rejected_unknown` → LCM raises `LockOperationFailed` and keeps the repair open. This is the identical mechanism we verified end-to-end for the *set* path in #1397.
3. LCM even runs `_async_uc_reconcile_value_db(10)` on that failure path — a fresh single-slot read that would scrub the stale cache entry — but that read is best-effort and faces the same coin-flip odds. It evidently timed out too: the new diagnostics still show `10: pin#0eafe084` on the back door.

The diagnostics corroborate the mesh diagnosis independently: **both** locks re-suspended slot 5, and the PR #1410 link-health sentence baked into those repairs reads "80 commands reached this lock… **39 read requests went unanswered**" (back door) and 32/66 on the front door. Same ~50% loss we measured in #1397's controlled test.

Worth remembering: the slot-10 code is almost certainly **not on the lock at all**. flyize set the slot to Available in zwave-js-ui back in June and the code never worked on the keypad — it's a stale driver value-DB entry. One successful fresh read of slot 10 erases it (`persistUserCode` overwrites on an Available report). Hard refresh and re-interview "didn't work" for the same reason the clear didn't: the reads keep timing out. It's plausible slot 10 specifically never gets refreshed because the bulk `ExtendedUserCodeGet` chain breaks mid-sequence before reaching it, while slots 1–5 (early in the chain) refresh fine — though per-slot timeouts alone explain it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A lossy link poisons *both* directions of cache repair: the write can't be verified (so it reports failure even if it landed) **and** the read that would scrub the stale value never returns (so the phantom persists). That's why three different remedies — clear, hard refresh, re-interview — all "fail" identically.
- `ERROR_UNKNOWN` from the driver is not evidence the device rejected anything; for a no-Supervision lock it literally means "I couldn't confirm." HA's translation ("the device rejected the credential") overstates what's known — worth keeping in mind when reading user reports.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The same timeouts are why hard refresh and re-interview didn't scrub it: any *successful* fresh read of slot 10 would.
